headline: New lead in Sagar-Runi case: Cultural figure linked to murders after 14 years
summary: Chief Prosecutor of the International Crimes Tribunal says a connection was found via call detail records during an investigation into another case.
details: The Chief Prosecutor of the International Crimes Tribunal, Md. Aminul Islam, has claimed that a cultural figure is linked to the murder of journalist couple Sagar Sarwar and Meherun Runi.
The lead emerged after the tribunal's investigation agency reviewed call detail records (CDR) while investigating a separate case.
Sagar Sarwar, news editor of Maasranga Television, and Meherun Runi, senior reporter of ATN Bangla, were brutally killed in their rented home in West Rajabazar, Dhaka, on February 11, 2012.
Chief Prosecutor Aminul Islam clarified that the tribunal's agency is not the primary investigator for the Sagar-Runi case, as that is handled by the PBI.
He stated that while working as an investigation agency, they may uncover clues to other events, and they are currently verifying the findings.
If authentic evidence is found after further investigation, the information will be shared with the PBI investigation officer to assist the case.
The Chief Prosecutor also noted that the murder is a separate case and not a widespread or systematic crime, meaning it will be be tried in the relevant sessions court rather than the tribunal.
caption:
A new lead has emerged in the 14-year-old Sagar-Runi murder case, linking a cultural figure to the crime.

The Chief Prosecutor of the International Crimes Tribunal, Md. Aminul Islam, has claimed that a cultural figure is linked to the murder of journalist couple Sagar Sarwar and Meherun Runi.

The lead emerged after the tribunal's investigation agency reviewed call detail records (CDR) while investigating a separate case.

Sagar Sarwar, news editor of Maasranga Television, and Meherun Runi, senior reporter of ATN Bangla, were brutally killed in their rented home in West Rajabazar, Dhaka, on February 11, 2012.

Chief Prosecutor Aminul Islam clarified that the tribunal's agency is not the primary investigator for the Sagar-Runi case, as that is handled by the PBI.

He stated that while working as an investigation agency, they may uncover clues to other events, and they are currently verifying the findings.

If authentic evidence is found after further investigation, the information will be shared with the PBI investigation officer to assist the case.

The Chief Prosecutor also noted that the murder is a separate case and not a widespread or systematic crime, meaning it will be be tried in the relevant sessions court rather than the tribunal.

headline_marked: ACC [[summons ex-army chief Shafiuddin Ahmed]] over corruption allegations
headline: ACC summons ex-army chief Shafiuddin Ahmed over corruption allegations
summary: The Anti-Corruption Commission has ordered the former Army Chief to appear for questioning regarding the acquisition of illegal assets.
details: The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) has summoned former Army Chief General S M Shafiuddin Ahmed to be questioned regarding allegations of acquiring illegal assets through corruption.
ACC Deputy Director Mo. Aktarul Islam confirmed the summons on Sunday, stating that an investigation is currently underway into various irregularities and corruption charges.
General Shafiuddin Ahmed has been directed to appear at the ACC head office on September 14, along with a photocopy of his National Identity Card (NID).
A two-member investigation team has been formed to conduct the probe. The team is led by ACC Director Mo. Abul Hasnat and includes Deputy Director Mozammel Hossain.
The commission has stated that hearing the former Army Chief's statement is essential for a fair and thorough investigation into the assets and irregularities.
caption:
Former Army Chief General S M Shafiuddin Ahmed has been summoned by the ACC for questioning on illegal assets.

The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) has summoned former Army Chief General S M Shafiuddin Ahmed to be questioned regarding allegations of acquiring illegal assets through corruption.

ACC Deputy Director Mo. Aktarul Islam confirmed the summons on Sunday, stating that an investigation is currently underway into various irregularities and corruption charges.

General Shafiuddin Ahmed has been directed to appear at the ACC head office on September 14, along with a photocopy of his National Identity Card (NID).

A two-member investigation team has been formed to conduct the probe. The team is led by ACC Director Mo. Abul Hasnat and includes Deputy Director Mozammel Hossain.

The commission has stated that hearing the former Army Chief's statement is essential for a fair and thorough investigation into the assets and irregularities.
